title.rendered: Abide in the Vine: Fruit Comes from Union, Not Effort | Living from Rest, Day 10

excerpt.rendered: Jesus said apart from Me you can do nothing. Day 10 of Living from Rest looks at the one word that holds the Christian life together: abide.

content.rendered:
A branch does not strain to produce grapes. It simply stays in the vine. Fruitfulness is a by-product of a connection, not the achievement of a performer.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, November 10, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 10

Today’s Scripture

“Abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in Me. I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing.”
John 15:4-5 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

John 15 is the clearest picture of rest-based fruitfulness in the New Testament. It is the night before Jesus goes to the cross, and He gives His disciples one word to carry everything else they will ever do for Him: abide. Not strive. Not perform. Not hustle. Abide. Stay. Remain. Live inside the union.

John 15:5, in the NKJV, says, “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing.” The AMPC says, “Whoever lives in Me and I in him bears much (abundant) fruit. However, apart from Me [cut off from vital union with Me] you can do nothing.” The TPT says, “I am the sprouting vine and you’re my branches. As you live in union with me as your source, fruitfulness will stream from within you, but when you live separated from me you are powerless.”

Three truths flow from this picture. First, fruit is not forced. A grape does not grow because the branch tried hard. The branch stays attached, and the life of the vine produces the fruit. Second, the branch cannot do it alone. “Without Me you can do nothing.” That line is absolute. Not little. Not a little less than you would like. Nothing. Third, the branch does not have to carry the vine. The vine carries the branch. The branch simply receives.

Abiding, in practice, is not mystical. It is daily. It is time in the Word. It is prayer that is not just transaction. It is quiet obedience in small matters. It is confession when you sin, and reception of grace when you confess. It is a steady, unhurried attention to Jesus. It is picking up the phone, metaphorically, every time your heart drifts, and saying, “Lord, thank You that I am in You and You are in me. Your life is growing in me.”

If you have been striving to produce fruit for Jesus, John 15 is for you. Fruit is not what you give Him. Fruit is what He grows out of you when you abide. Lay down the striving. Rest in the union He has already made. You are the branch. He is the Vine. He is more than able to do through you what you were never meant to do apart from Him.

What Abiding Looks Like Today

Steady attention. Word, prayer, quiet, obedience, confession, communion.

Dependent thanksgiving. You thank Him for His life in you before you take your work to the world.

Receiving fruit, not forcing it. You trust the Vine to produce what the branch cannot.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You that I am a branch in the True Vine. I abide in You and You abide in me, just as You said in John 15:5. Thank You that I do not have to force fruit; Your life in me produces it. Today I acknowledge my union with You and I walk in it. Apart from You I can do nothing; in You I bear much fruit. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
